## Overview

WISE-APP connects to a data directory on a local or remote file system. The directory contains three top-level components: **metadata**, **microdata**, and **hazard** data. Microdata and hazard data are spatially linked using the [H3 spatial indexing system](https://h3geo.org), which maps survey locations to hexagonal grid cells shared with the weather and events data.

## Data sources

The following data sources are currently included in WISE-APP:

### Global Monitoring Database (GMD)
The GMD is a harmonised collection of nationally representative household surveys from 150+ low- and middle-income countries, covering 1990–2023. It includes over 1,000 survey waves and 20 million households, with detailed welfare and demographic variables.

WISE-APP uses a subset of GMD surveys that have been geocoded and timestamped to enable spatial and temporal linkage with hazard data. Individual and household-level microdata are included where available, along with a spatial lookup file.

The following surveys from GMD are currently available in WISE-APP, with more to be added in future releases.:
*Add drop down list of surveys here based on `survey_list.csv`*

based on data quality, spatial coverage, and temporal alignment with hazard data. The sample includes 100+ surveys across 50+ countries, with a focus on sub-Saharan Africa.

### ERA5-Land climate reanalysis
ERA5-Land is a high-resolution global climate reanalysis dataset produced by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). It provides hourly estimates of 20+ weather variables at a spatial resolution of 9 km, covering the period 1950–2024. ERA5-Land is widely used in climate impact research due to its high quality and consistency.

WISE-APP uses monthly aggregates of selected ERA5-Land variables, spatially indexed by H3 cells. 
*Add drop down with list of weather variables available*

### CMIP6 climate projections
The Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) is a coordinated effort among climate modeling centers worldwide to produce standardized climate projections under different greenhouse gas emissions scenarios. WISE-APP uses CMIP6 projections for 2015–2100 under three shared socioeconomic pathways (SSPs): SSP 2-4.5, SSP 3-7.0, and SSP 5-8.5. Multiple model runs are included to capture uncertainty in climate projections.

WISE-APP applies a delta method to perturb historical weather observations using CMIP6 change fields, producing future weather scenarios that reflect both historical variability and projected climate change. The same set of weather variables is available for both historical and future simulations.

## Directory Structure

```
data/
├── metadata/
│   ├── survey_list.csv
│   ├── variable_list.csv
│   └── cpi_ppp.csv
│
├── microdata/
│   ├── hh/{code}/
│   ├── ind/{code}/
│   ├── firm/{code}/
│   └── h3/{code}/
│
└── hazard/
    ├── weather/
    │   ├── historical/{code}/
    │   └── projections/{code}/
    └── events/
        ├── historical/{code}/
        └── probabilistic/{code}/
```

`{code}` is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code (e.g. `GNB`, `NGA`, `ETH`).

The data directory can be stored locally or on a supported remote file system: AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Data Lake, Hugging Face, or Databricks.

## Metadata

Three small CSV files are loaded once when WISE-APP connects to the data directory. They drive UI filtering, variable labelling, and monetary comparability adjustments.

### `survey_list.csv`

One row per survey–level combination for which a microdata file exists.

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `economy` | string | Economy name |
| `code` | string | Country code |
| `year` | integer | Starting year of survey |
| `survname` | string | Survey acronym (e.g. `EHCVM`, `LSMS`) |
| `level` | string | Unit of observation: `hh`, `ind`, or `firm` |
| `obs` | integer | Number of observations |
| `source` | string | Data source |

### `variable_list.csv`

One row per variable. Controls which variables appear in the UI, how they are labelled, and how they are used in modelling.

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `name` | string | Variable name as it appears in the microdata |
| `label` | string | Human-readable label shown in the UI |
| `type` | string | R data type: `numeric`, `integer`, `logical`, `factor`, `character`, `Date` |
| `units` | string | Unit of measurement (e.g. `LCU/day`, `years`, `mm`) |
| `id` | binary | 1 if ID, date, or other special variable |
| `outcome` | binary | 1 if outcome of interest |
| `hazard` | binary | 1 if hazard/weather variable |
| `ind` | binary | 1 if measured at individual level |
| `hh` | binary | 1 if measured at household level |
| `firm` | binary | 1 if measured at firm level |
| `area` | binary | 1 if measured at area level |
| `interact` | binary | 1 if available as an interaction term in the model |
| `fe` | binary | 1 if available as a fixed effect in the model |

The following variables must be present: `code`, `economy`, `year`, `survname`, `int_year`, `int_month`, `loc_id`, `h3`, `timestamp`, at least one outcome variable, and at least one hazard variable.

### `cpi_ppp.csv`

One row per country–year–data level. Used to convert welfare aggregates from local currency units to comparable 2021 PPP USD.

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `code` | string | Country code |
| `year` | integer | Starting year of survey |
| `data_level` | string | Geographic level of price data (e.g. `national`, `urban`, `rural`) |
| `cpi` | numeric | Consumer price index |
| `ppp2021` | numeric | PPP conversion factor relative to 2021 USD |

## Microdata

All microdata files are in **Parquet format**, named `{code}_{year}_{survname}_{source}_{level}.parquet` and stored under `microdata/{level}/{code}/`. For example:

```
microdata/hh/GNB/GNB_2018_EHCVM_GMD_hh.parquet
microdata/ind/GNB/GNB_2018_EHCVM_GMD_ind.parquet
microdata/firm/GNB/GNB_2018_EHCVM_GMD_firm.parquet
microdata/h3/GNB/GNB_2018_EHCVM_GMD_h3.parquet
```

All microdata files must include: `code`, `economy`, `year`, `survname`, `int_year`, `int_month`, `loc_id`, and at least one outcome variable.

### Household file — `_hh.parquet`

One row per household. Key columns include `hhid`, `welfare` (welfare per day), `hhsize`, interview date fields, and spatial unit `loc_id`.

### Individual file — `_ind.parquet`

One row per individual. Key columns include `hhid`, `pid`, `wage` (wage per day), `age`, interview date fields, and `loc_id`.

### Firm file — `_firm.parquet`

One row per firm. Key columns include `fid`, `revenue` (revenue per day), `employees`, interview date fields, and `loc_id`.

### H3 lookup file — `_h3.parquet`

One row per H3 cell per location. This is the **spatial bridge** between microdata and all hazard data — a single H3 file covers both `_hh.parquet` and `_ind.parquet` from the same survey. Required columns are `code`, `year`, `survname`, `loc_id`, and `h3`. The optional `pop_2020` column (GHS-POP 2020 population) is used to weight hazard variables within locations when available.

H3 cell indices are stored as hexadecimal strings (e.g. `8928308280fffff`) but are 64-bit integers under the hood. Cell resolution is not fixed — merges are performed across resolutions using H3 parent/child relationships.

## Hazard Data

All hazard files are in **Parquet format**, spatially indexed using H3 cells and temporally indexed at monthly resolution. The H3 index is the join key to the `_h3.parquet` lookup, which maps H3 cells to `loc_id` in the microdata.

### Weather — Historical

Stored under `hazard/weather/historical/{code}/`. One row per H3 cell per month, covering the full historical record of the source dataset.

Filename: `{code}_{source}.parquet` — e.g. `GNB_era5land.parquet`, `GNB_chirps3.parquet`.

Key columns: `h3`, `timestamp` (first day of month), plus weather variables such as `t` (monthly temperature °C), `tx` (daily maximum temperature °C), `spei6` (6-month SPEI), and others.

### Weather — Projected

Stored under `hazard/weather/projections/{code}/`. Same schema as historical weather, plus a `model` column for multi-model ensembles (e.g. CMIP6).

Filename: `{code}_{source}_{scenario}.parquet` — e.g.:

```
GNB_cmip6_historical.parquet   # historical simulation (1950–2014)
GNB_cmip6_ssp245.parquet       # SSP 2-4.5 (2015–2100)
GNB_cmip6_ssp370.parquet       # SSP 3-7.0 (2015–2100)
GNB_cmip6_ssp585.parquet       # SSP 5-8.5 (2015–2100)
```

The historical scenario covers 1950–2014 and the SSP scenarios cover 2015–2100. These are used together to compute climate change deltas applied in the Simulate Welfare step.

### Events

> **Under development — not yet implemented in WISE-APP.**

Historical and probabilistic event data (e.g. floods, cyclones) are planned for a future release. Historical event files will contain one row per H3 cell per discrete event; probabilistic files will contain one row per H3 cell per return period.

## Spatial Integration: H3

WISE-APP uses the [H3 spatial indexing system](https://h3geo.org) to flexibly join microdata and hazard data:

- Survey microdata files include `loc_id` (unique spatial unit), `int_year`, and `int_month`.
- H3 lookup files map each `loc_id` to one or more H3 hexagon cell IDs.
- Hazard files include `h3` and `timestamp`, matched to survey locations and interview dates via the H3 lookup.

One or more survey observations are mapped to a spatial unit `loc_id`, which is represented by one or more H3 hexagons. Merges across H3 resolutions are handled using H3 parent/child relationships.
